art_instructions: Inside the bright, cozy Greek classroom, place a low honey-colored oak student desk near a large sunlit window on soft blue walls with wooden beams and a colorful woven rug beneath. Seat Koala at the desk, three-quarters turned to the right, shown from the waist up so the tabletop is fully visible; she has soft gray fur, big fluffy ears, a charcoal nose, and wears her leaf-green scarf, with her tiny acorn-brown backpack hanging from the chair back. Koala’s right paw points clearly to the desktop and her mouth is open mid-speech (as if saying “ἰδού”), while her face shows calm curiosity and confidence—she is not afraid. On the desk top, place exactly three small gray-brown mice clearly on the surface in front of an open picture book: arrange them in a neat row, evenly spaced for easy counting, all the same size; one stands on hind legs sniffing, one sits with tail curled, and one walks toward the book margin. Make sure all three mice are entirely on the table, not touching Koala, and illuminated by the natural light so they stand out. Include a blue-and-white ceramic cup with pencils on the left side of the desk and the open book centered behind the mice. Keep the teacher’s simple podium and a hint of another low desk softly out of focus in the background to reinforce the classroom setting.
